pr.title: fix: skip empty matches at a chunk boundary inside removed content
pr.body:
Since #359, an empty match inside removed content is skipped by `replace` and `replaceAll`. That only holds while no chunk boundary sits at the match: removing the same range in two calls gives the same output but a different result.

```js
new MagicString('abcd').remove(1, 3).replaceAll('', '-').toString()            // '-a--d-'
new MagicString('abcd').remove(1, 2).remove(2, 3).replaceAll('', '-').toString() // '-a---d-'

new MagicString('abcd').remove(1, 3).replace(/(?=c)/, '-').toString()            // 'ad'
new MagicString('abcd').remove(1, 2).remove(2, 3).replace(/(?=c)/, '-').toString() // 'a-d'
```

Any split at the match does the same, including one from an earlier `appendLeft(2, '')`.

`_hasRemovedContent(start, end)` walks the chunks from the one at `start` while `chunk.start < end`. For an empty range on a boundary, `start === end === chunk.start`, so the loop never runs and the match is reported as present. Inside a chunk the search finds the chunk containing `start` instead, whose start is before `end`, which is why the unsplit case works.

This handles that one case: an empty range at a chunk boundary is removed when the chunks on both sides of it are. That is the same rule the unsplit case already follows, and it keeps the existing behaviour at the edges of a removed range (`[0, 1, 3, 4]` in the #359 test) and at the ends of the string.

I checked it exhaustively against that rule: every string of length 1 to 6, no removal or every combination of one or two `remove()` calls, and every set of no-op splits, comparing the indices passed to a `replaceAll('', fn)` replacer and to a `replaceAll(/x*/g, fn)` replacer. That is 19,761 cases; 17,070 disagree with the rule on master and none do with this change. A random fuzz of the other methods (chunk-split invariance, `clone()`, self-consistency of `lastChar`/`lastLine`/`isEmpty`/`hasChanged`) gives identical results before and after.

Three tests are added, all failing on master. The suite goes from 454 to 457 and ESLint is clean; `tsc` reports the same 23 errors as master, none in the changed files.

test_patch:
diff --git a/tests/MagicString/replace-all.test.ts b/tests/MagicString/replace-all.test.ts
index d8af99c..edbc025 100644
--- a/tests/MagicString/replace-all.test.ts
+++ b/tests/MagicString/replace-all.test.ts
@@ -175,6 +175,29 @@ describe('magicString', () => {
       assert.deepEqual(indexes, [0, 1, 3, 4])
     })
 
+    it('skips empty matches between two removed ranges', () => {
+      // removing [1, 3) in two steps leaves a chunk boundary at 2, which is
+      // still inside removed content
+      const removed = () => new MagicString('abcd').remove(1, 2).remove(2, 3)
+      const indexes: number[] = []
+
+      assert.strictEqual(removed().replaceAll('', '-').toString(), '-a--d-')
+      assert.strictEqual(removed().replaceAll(/x*/g, '-').toString(), '-a--d-')
+
+      removed().replaceAll('', (_match, index) => {
+        indexes.push(index)
+        return '-'
+      })
+      assert.deepEqual(indexes, [0, 1, 3, 4])
+    })
+
+    it('skips empty matches inside removed content after a split', () => {
+      const removed = () => new MagicString('abcd').appendLeft(2, '').remove(1, 3)
+
+      assert.strictEqual(removed().replaceAll('', '-').toString(), '-a--d-')
+      assert.strictEqual(removed().replaceAll(/x*/g, '-').toString(), '-a--d-')
+    })
+
     it('finds removed content that lies before the last searched chunk', () => {
       // the insert at 5 leaves the chunk search past the removed range, so the
       // lookup for a match inside it has to walk backwards to find it
diff --git a/tests/MagicString/replace.test.ts b/tests/MagicString/replace.test.ts
index a3f5568..2adeb63 100644
--- a/tests/MagicString/replace.test.ts
+++ b/tests/MagicString/replace.test.ts
@@ -339,5 +339,12 @@ describe('magicString', () => {
       assert.strictEqual(new MagicString('00').remove(0, 2).replace('0', '1').toString(), '')
       assert.strictEqual(new MagicString('00').remove(0, 2).replace(/0/, '1').toString(), '')
     })
+
+    it('skips an empty match between two removed ranges', () => {
+      // the lookahead matches at 2, which is removed whether [1, 3) went in one
+      // call or two
+      assert.strictEqual(new MagicString('abcd').remove(1, 3).replace(/(?=c)/, '-').toString(), 'ad')
+      assert.strictEqual(new MagicString('abcd').remove(1, 2).remove(2, 3).replace(/(?=c)/, '-').toString(), 'ad')
+    })
   })
 })

pr.title: fix: don't treat chunks emptied by an overwrite as removed in `replace`
pr.body:
Since #352, `replace()` and `replaceAll()` skip a match that lands on removed content, and `_hasRemovedContent()` decides that by looking for an empty chunk in the matched range. `update()` and `overwrite()` leave empty chunks too: when the range spans several chunks, the replacement goes on the first one and the others are emptied. Their text was replaced, not removed, but a match over them is skipped all the same. So whether a match is replaced depends on whether some earlier edit happened to split the range, which the caller cannot see.

### Reproductions

All checked against current master (`magic-string@1.4.3`).

The only difference between these two is a split that inserts nothing:

```js
const a = new MagicString('aa')
a.update(0, 2, 'Q')
a.replaceAll(/a+/g, 'P')
a.toString() // 'P'

const b = new MagicString('aa')
b.appendLeft(1, '')
b.update(0, 2, 'Q')
b.replaceAll(/a+/g, 'P')
b.toString() // 'Q', expected 'P'
```

The same happens with `replace()`, with a string pattern, and with `overwrite()` in place of `update()`. Any earlier edit that splits the range has this effect, not only an empty insert:

```js
new MagicString('abcd').remove(0, 1).update(0, 2, 'Q').replace('ab', 'P').toString()
// 'Qcd', expected 'Pcd': 'ab' was overwritten after the removal, not removed
```

A range that an earlier `replaceAll()` overwrote cannot be matched again either:

```js
const s = new MagicString('aa')
s.appendLeft(1, '')
s.replaceAll(/a+/g, 'P')
s.replaceAll(/a+/g, 'Q').toString() // 'P', and 'Q' without the split
```

### The fix

`update()` now records on the chunks it empties where the overwritten range starts, and on the first chunk where the range ends (`replacedFrom` and `replacesUntil` on `Chunk`). `remove()` and `reset()` clear both, a split keeps `replacedFrom` on both halves, and `clone()` copies them. `_hasRemovedContent()` treats an emptied chunk as present when the match includes the first chunk of that overwrite and that chunk's replacement still reaches it. Removed chunks, trimmed ones and ranges overwritten with `''` are unaffected.

Both conditions matter:

- A match that leaves the first chunk out is still skipped. After `update(0, 3, 'Q')` on `'abc'` split at 1, `replace('bc', 'P')` still gives `'Q'`. Overwriting only the emptied chunks would leave `'Q'` in place and add `'P'` after it. Without the split, the same call throws `cannot split a chunk that has already been edited`.
- After such a split, the first chunk can be edited again on its own, and its replacement then no longer stands for the rest of the range. In the same example, `update(0, 1, 'R')` or `reset(0, 1)` followed by `replace('abc', 'P')` still gives `'R'` or `'a'`. Recording only where the range starts would bring those chunks back. With an empty replacement it would even make the result depend on the split again, since `update(0, 2, '')` followed by `update(0, 1, 'Y')` can be reached with or without it.

One consequence to be aware of: a match that includes the first chunk but ends inside the range is now replaced, and the rest of the range loses its replacement, as it does when `overwrite()` is called on that part directly. Master already did this when the match ended exactly where the first chunk ends, and skipped the match when it ended further in. So on `'abc'`, `update(0, 3, 'Q')` then `replace('ab', 'P')` gives `'P'` with a split at 2 and `'Q'` with a split at 1 (and throws with none). This branch gives `'P'` for both. Skipping both would also be consistent, but it changes far more existing results (2,588 against 144 in the comparison below), because the first case is the common one.

### Evidence

The same metamorphic fuzz as in #361: random sequences of edits on random strings, each run with and without a few `appendLeft(k, '')` splits, comparing `toString()`, `slice()`, `lastChar()`, `lastLine()`, `isEmpty()`, `hasChanged()` and `length()`. Divergences from `replace()`/`replaceAll()`:

| run | master | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200,000 trials, every edit method plus `replace`/`replaceAll` | 4 | 0 |
| 200,000 trials, inserts, `update`, `overwrite`, `remove`, `replace`, `replaceAll` | 27 | 0 |

With #361 merged, these are the only divergences left on master in both runs.

The fuzz never uses an empty replacement and never trims one away, so I also checked exhaustively on `'abcde'`: every sequence of one or two edits (`remove`, `update` with content, `update` with `''`, `reset`) over every range, under every placement of zero, one or two empty inserts, followed by `replace`/`replaceAll` of every substring, as a string and as a RegExp, 1,811,700 cases in all. Each result is compared with the one without the inserts, and each skip decision with a per-character model of which text is still represented in the output (the model's rendering matched `toString()` in every case):

| | master | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cases where nothing throws | 1,650,048 | 1,649,452 |
| result depends on the empty inserts | 18,100 | 0 |
| skip decision differs from the model | 64,716 | 0 |

The 596 cases that now throw are matches that master skipped and that also end inside another overwritten chunk, so overwriting them throws `cannot split a chunk that has already been edited`. The same calls throw on master as well when the range is not split.

A second exhaustive check runs `trim()`, `trimStart()`, `trimEnd()` or `trimLines()` between the edits and the replace, with whitespace replacements that the trim can empty: 228,830 of 6,436,950 comparisons depend on the inserts on master, 0 on this branch.

On the same random trials, 145 of 355,590 runs give a different result than on master. 142 of them are matches that master skipped and this branch replaces, as described above. In one trial (2 runs) a later `replaceAll('a', 'P')` now throws `cannot split a chunk that has already been edited`, because it falls inside a range that a partial match before it now replaces. One run no longer throws.

3 tests added: two fail on master, and the third pins down the matches that must still be skipped. The 454 existing tests pass unchanged. Lint is clean, and `pnpm run typecheck` reports the same `TS2341` errors as on master.

This touches `_hasRemovedContent()` like #366, which fixes empty matches at a chunk boundary inside removed content. The two only conflict in the test file, where both add a test at the end of the same block. I checked the combination: all 460 tests pass, the fuzz runs above show no divergences, and both exhaustive checks (and the one from #366) report 0.

fix: don't treat chunks emptied by an overwrite as removed in `replace`

Since #352, `replace()` and `replaceAll()` skip a match that lands on removed content, and `_hasRemovedContent()` decides that by looking for an empty chunk in the matched range. `update()` and `overwrite()` leave empty chunks too: when the range spans several chunks, the replacement goes on the first one and the others are emptied. Their text was replaced, not removed, but a match over them is skipped all the same. So whether a match is replaced depends on whether some earlier edit happened to split the range, which the caller cannot see.

### Reproductions

All checked against current master (`magic-string@1.4.3`).

The only difference between these two is a split that inserts nothing:

```js
const a = new MagicString('aa')
a.update(0, 2, 'Q')
a.replaceAll(/a+/g, 'P')
a.toString() // 'P'

const b = new MagicString('aa')
b.appendLeft(1, '')
b.update(0, 2, 'Q')
b.replaceAll(/a+/g, 'P')
b.toString() // 'Q', expected 'P'
```

The same happens with `replace()`, with a string pattern, and with `overwrite()` in place of `update()`. Any earlier edit that splits the range has this effect, not only an empty insert:

```js
new MagicString('abcd').remove(0, 1).update(0, 2, 'Q').replace('ab', 'P').toString()
// 'Qcd', expected 'Pcd': 'ab' was overwritten after the removal, not removed
```

A range that an earlier `replaceAll()` overwrote cannot be matched again either:

```js
const s = new MagicString('aa')
s.appendLeft(1, '')
s.replaceAll(/a+/g, 'P')
s.replaceAll(/a+/g, 'Q').toString() // 'P', and 'Q' without the split
```

### The fix

`update()` now records on the chunks it empties where the overwritten range starts, and on the first chunk where the range ends (`replacedFrom` and `replacesUntil` on `Chunk`). `remove()` and `reset()` clear both, a split keeps `replacedFrom` on both halves, and `clone()` copies them. `_hasRemovedContent()` treats an emptied chunk as present when the match includes the first chunk of that overwrite and that chunk's replacement still reaches it. Removed chunks, trimmed ones and ranges overwritten with `''` are unaffected.

Both conditions matter:

- A match that leaves the first chunk out is still skipped. After `update(0, 3, 'Q')` on `'abc'` split at 1, `replace('bc', 'P')` still gives `'Q'`. Overwriting only the emptied chunks would leave `'Q'` in place and add `'P'` after it. Without the split, the same call throws `cannot split a chunk that has already been edited`.
- After such a split, the first chunk can be edited again on its own, and its replacement then no longer stands for the rest of the range. In the same example, `update(0, 1, 'R')` or `reset(0, 1)` followed by `replace('abc', 'P')` still gives `'R'` or `'a'`. Recording only where the range starts would bring those chunks back. With an empty replacement it would even make the result depend on the split again, since `update(0, 2, '')` followed by `update(0, 1, 'Y')` can be reached with or without it.

One consequence to be aware of: a match that includes the first chunk but ends inside the range is now replaced, and the rest of the range loses its replacement, as it does when `overwrite()` is called on that part directly. Master already did this when the match ended exactly where the first chunk ends, and skipped the match when it ended further in. So on `'abc'`, `update(0, 3, 'Q')` then `replace('ab', 'P')` gives `'P'` with a split at 2 and `'Q'` with a split at 1 (and throws with none). This branch gives `'P'` for both. Skipping both would also be consistent, but it changes far more existing results (2,588 against 144 in the comparison below), because the first case is the common one.

### Evidence

The same metamorphic fuzz as in #361: random sequences of edits on random strings, each run with and without a few `appendLeft(k, '')` splits, comparing `toString()`, `slice()`, `lastChar()`, `lastLine()`, `isEmpty()`, `hasChanged()` and `length()`. Divergences from `replace()`/`replaceAll()`:

| run | master | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200,000 trials, every edit method plus `replace`/`replaceAll` | 4 | 0 |
| 200,000 trials, inserts, `update`, `overwrite`, `remove`, `replace`, `replaceAll` | 27 | 0 |

With #361 merged, these are the only divergences left on master in both runs.

The fuzz never uses an empty replacement and never trims one away, so I also checked exhaustively on `'abcde'`: every sequence of one or two edits (`remove`, `update` with content, `update` with `''`, `reset`) over every range, under every placement of zero, one or two empty inserts, followed by `replace`/`replaceAll` of every substring, as a string and as a RegExp, 1,811,700 cases in all. Each result is compared with the one without the inserts, and each skip decision with a per-character model of which text is still represented in the output (the model's rendering matched `toString()` in every case):

| | master | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cases where nothing throws | 1,650,048 | 1,649,452 |
| result depends on the empty inserts | 18,100 | 0 |
| skip decision differs from the model | 64,716 | 0 |

The 596 cases that now throw are matches that master skipped and that also end inside another overwritten chunk, so overwriting them throws `cannot split a chunk that has already been edited`. The same calls throw on master as well when the range is not split.

A second exhaustive check runs `trim()`, `trimStart()`, `trimEnd()` or `trimLines()` between the edits and the replace, with whitespace replacements that the trim can empty: 228,830 of 6,436,950 comparisons depend on the inserts on master, 0 on this branch.

On the same random trials, 145 of 355,590 runs give a different result than on master. 142 of them are matches that master skipped and this branch replaces, as described above. In one trial (2 runs) a later `replaceAll('a', 'P')` now throws `cannot split a chunk that has already been edited`, because it falls inside a range that a partial match before it now replaces. One run no longer throws.

3 tests added: two fail on master, and the third pins down the matches that must still be skipped. The 454 existing tests pass unchanged. Lint is clean, and `pnpm run typecheck` reports the same `TS2341` errors as on master.

This touches `_hasRemovedContent()` like #366, which fixes empty matches at a chunk boundary inside removed content. The two only conflict in the test file, where both add a test at the end of the same block. I checked the combination: all 460 tests pass, the fuzz runs above show no divergences, and both exhaustive checks (and the one from #366) report 0.

diff --git a/tests/MagicString/replace-all.test.ts b/tests/MagicString/replace-all.test.ts
index edbc025..69e45bd 100644
--- a/tests/MagicString/replace-all.test.ts
+++ b/tests/MagicString/replace-all.test.ts
@@ -207,5 +207,17 @@ describe('magicString', () => {
       assert.strictEqual(create().replaceAll(/0/g, '1').toString(), '--!--')
       assert.strictEqual(create().replace('0', '1').toString(), '--!--')
     })
+
+    it('replaces matches over a range that one overwrite spread across several chunks', () => {
+      // the first pass overwrites 'aa', which the insert of nothing has split,
+      // and the second pass matches the same range again
+      const s = new MagicString('aa').appendLeft(1, '')
+      s.replaceAll(/a+/g, 'P')
+      assert.strictEqual(s.replaceAll(/a+/g, 'Q').toString(), 'Q')
+
+      assert.strictEqual(new MagicString('aa').appendLeft(1, '').overwrite(0, 2, 'Q').replaceAll('aa', 'P').toString(), 'P')
+      // any earlier edit can split the range, here the removal
+      assert.strictEqual(new MagicString('abcd').remove(0, 1).update(0, 2, 'Q').replaceAll('ab', 'P').toString(), 'Pcd')
+    })
   })
 })
diff --git a/tests/MagicString/replace.test.ts b/tests/MagicString/replace.test.ts
index 2adeb63..8699370 100644
--- a/tests/MagicString/replace.test.ts
+++ b/tests/MagicString/replace.test.ts
@@ -340,6 +340,33 @@ describe('magicString', () => {
       assert.strictEqual(new MagicString('00').remove(0, 2).replace(/0/, '1').toString(), '')
     })
 
+    it('replaces a match over a range that one overwrite spread across several chunks', () => {
+      // `appendLeft(1, '')` inserts nothing but splits the range, so the
+      // replacement is stored on the first chunk and the second is emptied,
+      // which must not count as removed
+      assert.strictEqual(new MagicString('aa').update(0, 2, 'Q').replace('aa', 'P').toString(), 'P')
+      const s = new MagicString('aa').appendLeft(1, '').update(0, 2, 'Q')
+      assert.strictEqual(s.clone().replace('aa', 'P').toString(), 'P')
+      assert.strictEqual(s.clone().replace(/a+/, 'P').toString(), 'P')
+
+      // the emptied chunk may itself be split afterwards
+      const t = new MagicString('aaa').appendLeft(1, '').overwrite(0, 3, 'Q').appendLeft(2, '')
+      assert.strictEqual(t.replace('aaa', 'P').toString(), 'P')
+    })
+
+    it('skips a match over the rest of an overwritten range when the replacement is left out or gone', () => {
+      const create = () => new MagicString('abc').appendLeft(1, '').update(0, 3, 'Q')
+
+      // the match leaves out the first chunk, so the replacement would be doubled
+      assert.strictEqual(create().replace('bc', 'P').toString(), 'Q')
+      // editing the first chunk on its own drops the replacement for the rest
+      assert.strictEqual(create().update(0, 1, 'R').replace('abc', 'P').toString(), 'R')
+      assert.strictEqual(create().reset(0, 1).replace('abc', 'P').toString(), 'a')
+      // and removed content stays removed
+      assert.strictEqual(create().remove(1, 3).replace('abc', 'P').toString(), 'Q')
+      assert.strictEqual(create().update(1, 3, '').replace('abc', 'P').toString(), 'Q')
+    })
+
     it('skips an empty match between two removed ranges', () => {
       // the lookahead matches at 2, which is removed whether [1, 3) went in one

pr.title: fix: shift replacesUntil and replacedFrom in Bundle#toMagicString
pr.body:
`toMagicString` adds each source's offset to `start` and `end` of the cloned chunks, but not to `replacesUntil` and `replacedFrom`, which a multi-chunk `overwrite` sets (#367) and which are also positions in that source's original. `replace` and `replaceAll` read them through `_hasRemovedContent`, so in any source after the first a match can be skipped as removed content, or the lookup misses and throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replacesUntil')`.

```js
const a = new MagicString('foo bar')
a.appendLeft(4, '')
a.overwrite(0, 7, 'baz')
const b = new Bundle({ separator: '' })
b.addSource(new MagicString('let '))
b.addSource(a)
const flat = b.toMagicString()
flat.replace('foo bar', 'qux')
flat.toString() // 'let baz', while the same edits on new MagicString('let foo bar') give 'let qux'
```

The test covers both cases and fails without the change.

Written with AI assistance (Claude); I have reviewed the change.

+    it('shifts a multi-chunk overwrite in a later source', () => {
+      const a = new MagicString('foo bar')
+      a.appendLeft(4, '')
+      a.overwrite(0, 7, 'baz')
+      const b = new Bundle({ separator: '' })
+      b.addSource(new MagicString('let '))
+      b.addSource(a)
+
+      const flat = b.toMagicString()
+      flat.replace('foo bar', 'qux')
+      assert.strictEqual(flat.toString(), 'let qux')
+
+      const c = new MagicString('xxyy zz')
+      c.appendLeft(4, '')
+      c.overwrite(2, 7, 'Q')
+      const b2 = new Bundle({ separator: '' })
+      b2.addSource(new MagicString('foo bar '))
+      b2.addSource(c)
+
+      const flat2 = b2.toMagicString()
+      flat2.replace(/o bar xxyy zz/, '!')
+      assert.strictEqual(flat2.toString(), 'fo!')
+    })
+
     it('keeps move() cycle-safety after flattening a moved source', () => {

pr.title: chore: enable strict type checking
pr.body:
Turns on `strict` in `tsconfig.json`. The chunk list is a doubly linked list looked up through `Map`s, so almost every method handles `Chunk | null | undefined`, which is the case strict null checks exist for. `tsc --strict` reported 50 errors on master. Several of them were on real defects:

- `move()` dereferenced `byStart.get(start)` without a check. An out-of-range `start` (e.g. `new MagicString('abc').move(5, 7, 0)`) threw a raw `TypeError`. It now throws a `MagicStringError`, and a test covers it.
- `update()` had an else-branch marked "unreachable" that a `NaN` index could still reach. That branch silently dropped the rest of the string, so it is removed. The branch was also the only reason to track `last`, so the range walk is now bounded by `end`.

The other sites only needed narrowing. Locals were re-typed rather than asserted. There are 5 new non-null assertions, each with a comment explaining why it holds. In `Bundle.toMagicString()` the `forEach` became a `for…of` so the compiler can follow the `first`/`last` assignments. `Bundle.getIndentString()` now counts with a `Map`.

There is no intended behaviour change apart from the `move()` error type. All 461 existing tests pass unchanged, plus the new one.

Plan: `plans/001-enable-strict-typescript.md` in #370. This will conflict with #373 in `move()`; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

This PR was created with the help of an agent.

pr.title: fix: reject non-integer and out-of-range indices consistently
pr.body:
The ten methods that take original-string indices each validated them differently. Some bad inputs corrupted the output silently instead of throwing. Results on v1.4.4:

| Call | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `new MagicString('abcdef').update(undefined, 2, 'X')` | `"abX"`: the rest of the string is lost and the map gets a `null` column | throws |
| `remove(NaN, 2)` | silent no-op | throws |
| `new MagicString('abc').appendLeft(100, 'X')` | `"Xabc"`, inserted at the *start* | throws |
| `appendLeft(-1, 'X')` | `"Xabc"` | `"abXc"`, counted from the end like `update`/`remove` |
| `move(5, 7, 0)` / `move(0, 3, 100)` | raw `TypeError` / silently moves to the end | throws `MagicStringError` |
| `appendRight(1.5, 'X')` | fractional column `1.5` in the sourcemap | throws |

A shared internal `_resolveIndex` now does the same thing in every method. It applies `offset`, counts a negative index from the end, and rejects non-integers. Each method still does its own bounds check, so every existing error message is unchanged. `slice` still clamps like `String.prototype.slice`. The README documents the rule under `s.offset`.

Two tests encoded the old behaviour and are rewritten: "should append/prepend at end of string when index is out of upper bound" (from #302) asserted `'ABxCD'`, which means the `*Left` inserts landed at the start, contradicting the test's own title. They now assert a throw, and a new test covers `index === length`. Because out-of-range `append*`/`prepend*`/`move` calls now throw instead of misplacing content, this probably deserves a minor release rather than a patch.

Includes the `move()` bounds guard from #371 so this PR stands alone; whichever of the two lands second needs a small rebase. Plan: `plans/003-validate-indices-consistently.md` in #370.

This PR was created with the help of an agent.

pr.title: fix: keep the stored name when an overwritten range was split
pr.body:
`overwrite(…, { storeName: true })` stores the original text in `names`, and the replacement's mapping segment should point at it. Two paths broke that link:

- **The range was split by an earlier edit.** The mapping lookup used `names.indexOf(chunk.original)`, but `chunk.original` is only the first chunk's slice of the range. So `s.remove(3, 4); s.overwrite(0, 7, 'baz', { storeName: true })` on `'foo.bar'` gave `names: ['foo.bar']` with a segment that had no name index. Any earlier insert or edit inside the range triggers this. The lookup now uses `original.slice(chunk.start, chunk.replacesUntil)`, which is exactly the string `update()` stored. `replacesUntil` was added in #367. The fix covers both `MagicString` and `Bundle`.
- **Legacy `overwrite(a, b, c, true)`.** `overwrite()` coerced `true` to `{}` before `update()` could see it, so there was no deprecation warning and `names` stayed empty. It now warns once and calls `update()` with `{ storeName: true, overwrite: true }`, which is what the boolean form meant before 0.20. `update(…, true)` is unchanged.

There are four new tests, and the first three check the result through `SourceMapConsumer` or the decoded segments. One is a split range in `MagicString`, one is a partially removed range, one is the legacy boolean on `overwrite`, and one is a split range in `Bundle`.

Plan: `plans/004-keep-store-name-across-split-chunks.md` in #370.

This PR was created with the help of an agent.

pr.title: fix(bundle): stop addSource mutating the caller's source description
pr.body:
`bundle.addSource({ content, … })` wrote `filename`, `ignoreList`, `indentExclusionRanges` and `separator` onto the caller's object and stored that same object. `trimStart()`/`trimEnd()` then rewrote its `separator`. When one description was reused across bundles:

- the second bundle used the first bundle's separator (`"a;x"` instead of `"a\nx"`)
- trimming one bundle stripped the separator from the other
- the caller's object picked up four keys it never set

`addSource` now builds its own internal record and stores that, with every field resolved once. Content is still shared by reference, as before, so the identity assertions in the existing tests still hold. Because the stored `separator` is now always a `string`, the eight `source.separator !== undefined ? source.separator : this.separator` fallbacks are gone, along with their `v8 ignore` comments. `Bundle.ts` stays at 100 % coverage.

There are three new tests (no mutation, no separator leak between bundles, no trim leak between bundles), and all three fail on master. The local `BundleInternals` test types in `addSource.test.ts` and `clone.test.ts` now match the record shape. No assertions changed.

Plan: `plans/005-copy-bundle-source-descriptions.md` in #370.

index bffdf79..cf5af96 100644
--- a/tests/Bundle/addSource.test.ts
+++ b/tests/Bundle/addSource.test.ts
@@ -1,14 +1,15 @@
-import type { ExclusionRange } from '../../src/index.ts'
+import type { MagicString as BaseMagicString, ExclusionRange } from '../../src/index.ts'
 import { assert, describe, it } from 'vitest'
 import { Bundle } from '../../src/index.ts'
 import { IntegrityCheckingMagicString as MagicString } from '../__utils/IntegrityCheckingMagicString.ts'
 
 interface BundleInternals extends Bundle {
   sources: Array<{
-    content: MagicString
-    filename?: string
-    ignoreList?: boolean
-    indentExclusionRanges?: ExclusionRange | ExclusionRange[]
+    content: BaseMagicString
+    filename: string | undefined
+    ignoreList: boolean | undefined
+    indentExclusionRanges: ExclusionRange | ExclusionRange[] | undefined
+    separator: string
   }>
 }
 
@@ -87,5 +88,26 @@ describe('bundle', () => {
       b.addSource(foo1)
       assert.doesNotThrow(() => b.addSource(foo2))
     })
+
+    it('does not mutate the description object it is given', () => {
+      const b = new Bundle({ separator: ';' })
+      const description = { content: new MagicString('x', { filename: 'x.js' }) }
+
+      b.addSource(description)
+
+      assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(description), ['content'])
+    })
+
+    it('does not share state between bundles given the same description', () => {
+      const description = { content: new MagicString('x') }
+      const b1 = new Bundle({ separator: ';' })
+      const b2 = new Bundle({ separator: '\n' })
+
+      b1.addSource(new MagicString('a')).addSource(description)
+      b2.addSource(new MagicString('a')).addSource(description)
+
+      assert.equal(b1.toString(), 'a;x')
+      assert.equal(b2.toString(), 'a\nx')
+    })
   })
 })

diff --git a/tests/Bundle/trim.test.ts b/tests/Bundle/trim.test.ts
index 2448ec6..28056e0 100644
--- a/tests/Bundle/trim.test.ts
+++ b/tests/Bundle/trim.test.ts
@@ -119,5 +119,19 @@ describe('bundle', () => {
       b.trimEnd()
       assert.equal(b.toString(), 'Y  \nX')
     })
+
+    it('does not trim the separator of a sibling bundle given the same description', () => {
+      const description = { content: new MagicString(''), separator: ' \n' }
+      const b1 = new Bundle()
+      const b2 = new Bundle()
+
+      b1.addSource(new MagicString('a')).addSource(description)
+      b2.addSource(new MagicString('a')).addSource(description)
+
+      b1.trimEnd()
+
+      assert.equal(b1.toString(), 'a')
+      assert.equal(b2.toString(), 'a \n')
+    })
   })
 })

pr.title: fix: respect indent exclusions on moved edits and CRLF bundle intros
pr.body:
Two indent fixes:

- **`indent({ exclude })` on a moved edited chunk.** For edited content, the exclusion check used `charIndex`, which is the previous chunk's end in *list* order. That only equals the chunk's start while nothing has been moved. So `s.overwrite(4, 7, 'X\\nY'); s.move(4, 7, 0); s.indent('  ', { exclude: [[4, 7]] })` on `'abc\\ndef'` indented the excluded replacement (`'  X\\n  Yabc\\n'`). The check now uses `chunk.start`. Excluded edited content also still updates the "next character starts a line" flag, as `indentPiece` would; without that, the text after it got indented mid-line. `Bundle.indent()` passes `indentExclusionRanges` through this path, so hoisted code in a bundle was affected too.
- **`Bundle.indent()` on a CRLF intro** indented the `\\r` of blank lines, using `/^[^\\n]/gm` where `MagicString.indent()` uses `/^[^\\r\\n]/gm`. It now uses the same pattern.

Each fix has a test that fails on master.

Plan: `plans/006-fix-indent-exclude-and-to-magic-string.md` in #370. The plan's step 3 (carrying `indentExclusionRanges` through `toMagicString()`) was dropped, because `MagicString.indent()` never reads its own ranges, so the problem it described doesn't exist. The shift of `replacesUntil`/`replacedFrom` the plan also covered already landed in #369.

This PR was created with the help of an agent.

pr.title: perf: cut allocations and quadratic lookups on the sourcemap and bundle paths
pr.body:
Removes six places that did work scaling with input size. One commit each:

- **Stored names**: `storedNames` is now a `Set`, and `names` is indexed by a `Map` built once per `generateMap`. This replaces the `Object.defineProperty` object plus a `names.indexOf` per renamed chunk, and `Bundle`'s `names.includes` dedupe. The `Set` also rules out prototype pollution, which is what the `defineProperty` workaround (#194) was for.
- **`Bundle.length()`** sums `length()` plus the intro and outro instead of building every source's `toString()`.
- **Range mappings**: the per-line arrays are allocated only for `hires: 'experimental-range'`. **Visible change:** `generateDecodedMap().rangeMappings` is now `undefined` in other modes, instead of `[[], [], …]`.
- **`indent({ exclude })`** marks excluded characters in the existing `BitSet` instead of an object with one key per character.
- **`toMagicString()`** copies only the sourcemap locations that are actually set (new `BitSet#forEach`), instead of testing every character. Locations past a source's end are still dropped, as before.
- **`uniqueSourceIndexByFilename`** is now a `Map`. A filename of `__proto__` used to skip the duplicate check and emit `{}` as a source index in the map.

Range-mode output is byte-identical. There are 4 new tests, and the one existing test that asserted the empty `rangeMappings` arrays is updated.

## Numbers

Node 24.18.1 on a 10-core Linux container, master `0c6698f` vs this branch rebased onto it.

**Many stored names.** This is the case the names change targets, and the repo benchmark doesn't exercise it (its `storeName` row stores a single name). I used an ad-hoc script that renames 5,000 distinct identifiers with `storeName: true`, then calls `generateMap({ hires: true })`. Times are the median of 15 calls, over 3 runs per build:

| | master | this PR | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `MagicString.generateMap`, 5,000 names | 32–44 ms | 6.1–8.5 ms | **~5–7×** |
| `Bundle.generateMap`, 10 sources × 500 names | 49–55 ms | 3.8–5.6 ms | **~10×** |

<details><summary>script</summary>

```js
const { default: MagicString, Bundle } = await import(process.argv[2]) // path to dist/index.mjs
const N = 5000
const src = Array.from({ length: N }, (_, i) => `const id${i} = ${i};`).join('\n')
const s = new MagicString(src)
for (const m of src.matchAll(/id\d+/g)) s.overwrite(m.index, m.index + m[0].length, 'x', { storeName: true })
const b = new Bundle()
for (let k = 0; k < 10; k++) {
  const part = Array.from({ length: 500 }, (_, i) => `let v${k}_${i} = 0;`).join('\n')
  const p = new MagicString(part, { filename: `${k}.js` })
  for (const m of part.matchAll(/v\d+_\d+/g)) p.overwrite(m.index, m.index + m[0].length, 'y', { storeName: true })
  b.addSource(p)
}
function median(fn, reps = 15) {
  fn()
  const t = []
  for (let r = 0; r < reps; r++) { const a = performance.now(); fn(); t.push(performance.now() - a) }
  return t.sort((x, y) => x - y)[reps >> 1]
}
console.log({ magicString_ms: median(() => s.generateMap({ hires: true })), bundle_ms: median(() => b.generateMap({ hires: true })) })
```
</details>

**`benchmark/magic-string.bench.ts`** (#380). I ran the `generateMap`, `reads` and `bundle` groups 5 times each, interleaving master and this branch. The table shows the median ops/s, with the min–max of the 5 runs in parentheses:

| Row | master | this PR | |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **bundle `length()`** | 455,432 (346,584–462,406) | **1,068,115** (968,511–1,194,999) | **2.3×** |
| bundle `generateMap lo-res` | 756 (591–786) | 985 (794–1,025) | +30 % |
| bundle `generateMap hires: true` | 110 (85–116) | 120 (102–123) | +9 % |
| `generateMap` hires: experimental-range | 3,950 (2,337–4,574) | 4,623 (3,836–4,690) | +17 % |
| `generateMap` lo-res, edits | 9,211 (4,472–9,620) | 10,186 (8,707–10,338) | +11 % |
| `generateDecodedMap`, edits | 12,838 (7,088–15,247) | 15,069 (12,631–15,308) | +17 % |
| `generateMap` hires: true | 1,277 | 1,207 | ≈ |
| `indent` | 4,110 | 3,963 | ≈ (±15–40 % rme on this row) |

The non-bold gains are close to the noise. The master ranges have low outliers, so treat these as "not slower" rather than precise speedups. The `indent` change shows only with large `exclude` ranges, which the benchmark doesn't use.

Plan: `plans/008-reduce-allocations-on-hot-paths.md` in #370.

pr.title: fix(attributes): set data on mixed node selections
pr.body: Fixes #5557. `.data()` setters currently return before visiting any element if a selection starts with a text node. Run the existing setter loop before the first-element getter check, so mixed `.contents()` selections update their elements and remain chainable. The two setter docstrings now describe their all-elements behavior. The regression exercises both key/value and object-map setters through a real mixed selection. It fails on the original code and passes after the change. Validation: `npm test` passes all lint/type checks and 800 tests; `npm run build` and a built ESM smoke test pass. The website dependencies and `astro sync` were needed for the repository-wide lint setup. Biome reports one pre-existing website CSS warning and a schema-version informational message. Build-generated package.json export ordering is excluded. Other Node versions were not run locally. Self-reviewed against main 0ab9a8e943bb86704ceb962770bc46647404ea45. Authored with OpenAI Codex assistance.

issue_texts.5557:
data() setters skip all elements when the selection starts with text Calling a `.data()` setter on a mixed selection returned by `.contents()` skips every element when the first node is text. ```js const $ = load('
text
'); const contents = $('div').contents(); contents.data('foo', 'bar'); console.log($('span').data('foo')); // undefined, expected 'bar' ``` The object-map setter has the same problem. Both setters also return `undefined` instead of the selection in this case. Existing behavior and tests set data on *all* elements when the selection starts with an element; the leading text should simply be skipped. Reproduced against main 0ab9a8e943bb86704ceb962770bc46647404ea45 on macOS / Node.js. Baseline attributes tests pass; a public API regression fails. Proposed fix: execute the existing setter iteration before applying the first-element check that is needed for getters. Correct the two setter docstrings which currently describe first-element-only behavior. Investigated with OpenAI Codex assistance.

pr.title: fix(attributes): guard style access on non-element nodes
pr.body: Fixes #5559. Reading `.prop('style')` from a text, comment or document node currently calls `Object.keys(undefined)` and throws. Guard non-elements as the adjacent element-only property getters already do, returning undefined consistently with `.css()` and empty selections. The regression uses real text/comment/document nodes and fails on the original implementation. Existing element style tests continue to verify named/indexed properties and length. Validation: `npm test` passes all 800 tests, ESLint, TypeScript and Biome checks; `git diff --check` passes. One pre-existing website CSS warning and schema-version informational message remain. Other Node versions were not run locally. Self-review: one element guard and one regression test, independently based on main. Authored with OpenAI Codex assistance.

issue_texts.5559:
prop(style) throws for text, comment and document nodes Reading `.prop('style')` on a text, comment, or document node throws `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object`. Other element-only property getters return undefined on these nodes, and `.css()` already returns undefined. ```js const $ = load('
text
'); $('div').contents().first().prop('style'); // throws $.root().prop('style'); // throws ``` Expected: undefined, as for an absent style property, rather than a crash while enumerating the undefined result of `.css()`. Reproduced against main 0ab9a8e943bb86704ceb962770bc46647404ea45 with the existing attributes Vitest suite. Proposed fix: apply the same element guard used by the adjacent tagName/href getters before constructing style properties. Investigated with OpenAI Codex assistance on macOS / Node.js.

pr.title: fix(traversing): isolate stop predicates for nested Until calls
pr.body: When a `nextUntil`, `prevUntil`, or `parentsUntil` stop callback invokes the same method, the nested call currently replaces and clears the outer stop predicate. For the reproduction in #5613, the outer traversal returns `['b', 'c', 'd']` instead of stopping before `#c` and returning `['b']`. Keep the stop predicate and its matcher local to each invocation. The existing selector filtering, per-start callback indexes, and result postprocessing stay in the shared matcher. Add twelve regression cases covering all three methods, successful nested calls, caught nested exceptions, calls after a predicate throws, and per-start indexes across nested calls. Fixes #5613. Validation on Node 22.22.3: - Final regression tests against unchanged main: nine expected failures (nested success, caught-exception, and nested multi-start cases for each method). - `npm run test:vi`: 842 tests passed across 15 files. - `npm run lint`: passed, including ESLint, TypeScript, and Biome. - `npm run build`: passed. - Website `npm run build` and `npm run check`: passed (39 files, zero diagnostics). - Commit hook (`lint-staged`) and `git diff --check`: passed. The full test suite needed permission to listen on localhost for its HTTP-server tests. Other Node versions are left to the repository's CI matrix.

pr.title: fix: preserve sources when insertion targets are empty
pr.body: Closes #5654. Calling insertBefore or insertAfter with an empty target currently removes the source nodes from the document. Resolve the targets before detaching the source and return an empty selection when there is nowhere to insert. This matches jQuery 4 behavior. Added six regression cases covering both methods with an unmatched selector, an empty selection, and an empty array. All six fail before the fix. Verified jQuery 4 behavior independently with JSDOM. Validation: 842 Vitest tests passed; npm run build and npm run lint passed (one existing website CSS warning). Website dependencies and generated Astro types were needed for the full lint check. Codex (GPT-6) assisted with investigation, implementation, regression tests, and this description. Prepared for maintainer review. ## Readiness verification — 2026-10-22 UTC Verified commit `b0fc10f55027313731ac4605457a30f62347a81d` against the current upstream diff and contribution guidance. No unresolved review threads or merge conflicts were present at this check. `npm test` passed (lint/type checks plus 842 Vitest tests), then `npm run build` passed. Windows / Node 24.20.0. The build reorders generated package exports, so an extra post-build lint detects that generated ordering; restoring only the build-generated `package.json` change returns the clean, initially linted checkout. No source changes were needed. The existing website CSS warning remains. `git diff --check` passes. Local verification is separate from upstream CI. [The upstream workflow](https://github.com/cheeriojs/cheerio/actions/runs/39446046570) still requires maintainer approval; it has not been counted as a successful run.

issue_texts.5654:
insertBefore and insertAfter remove source elements when the target is empty With Cheerio 1.2.0/current main, an insertion into an empty target removes the source element from its current document: ```js import { load } from 'cheerio'; const $ = load('
source
'); const result = $('span').insertBefore('.missing'); console.log(result.length); // 0 console.log($('main').html()); // '' -- source is lost ``` `insertAfter` behaves the same way. Empty Cheerio selections and empty target arrays also reproduce it. Expected: an empty result, with `source` still under `
`. I checked both methods against the repository's jQuery 4.0.0 dependency under JSDOM; both preserve the source when the selector matches nothing. Both methods call `this.remove()` before checking whether any targets exist. I have a focused patch that returns an empty selection first, plus six regression tests covering the two methods and three target forms. All six fail against the unchanged source. Environment: Windows, Node 24.20.0. AI disclosure: Codex (GPT-6) assisted with investigation, reproduction, regression tests, and writing this report.

pr.title: feat: export DOM node type guards (#5459)
pr.body: Fixes #5459 Re-export the `domhandler` node type guards (`isTag`, `isText`, `isComment`, `isCDATA`, `isDocument`, `isDirective`, `hasChildren`) from `cheerio/utils`, so consumers inspecting `.contents()` no longer need to depend on `domhandler`/`domelementtype` directly (which risks mismatched DOM versions, e.g. `domelementtype` 2 vs 3). ```ts import { isText } from 'cheerio/utils'; ``` Added tests for all seven guards against real nodes from `cheerio.load` (element, text, comment, CDATA in xmlMode, directive, document). Tests: `npm run test:vi` (843 passing), `npm run lint:ts`, `npm run lint:biome`.

pr.title: Add `doc.createMergePair()` + do not duck-type `<<` string keys as merge keys
pr.body:
Fixes #718

This is a breaking change for users who've been creating `<<` merge keys manually, as this will now need to get done with the `doc.createMergePair(...)` that's introduced here, rather than `doc.createPair('<<', ...)`.

Thus far, merge keys have been treated as string values that are special, which was a little broken. Let's instead represent them (internally) with `Symbol('<<')` values, so that e.g. `!!str <<` and `"<<"` are always treated as the plain strings that they should be.

pr.title: Fix JS type of self-referential mappings used as merge sources
pr.body:
This fixes a v3 regression from #664.

I'm not really sure why anyone would use a self-referential mapping as a merge source, but doing so should work.

problem_statement:
Fix JS type of self-referential mappings used as merge sources

This fixes a v3 regression from #664.

I'm not really sure why anyone would use a self-referential mapping as a merge source, but doing so should work.
test_patch:
diff --git a/tests/doc/anchors.ts b/tests/doc/anchors.ts
index eea915c..cc53847 100644
--- a/tests/doc/anchors.ts
+++ b/tests/doc/anchors.ts
@@ -456,6 +456,16 @@ y:
     expect(() => parse(src, { merge: true })).not.toThrow()
   })
 
+  test('merge with circular reference', () => {
+    const src = '- &a { a: *a, b: B }\n- { <<: *a, b: X }\n'
+    const res = parse(src, { merge: true })
+    expect(res[1].a instanceof Map).toBe(false)
+    expect(res).toEqual([
+      { a: res[0], b: 'B' },
+      { a: res[0], b: 'X' }
+    ])
+  })
+
   describe('parse errors', () => {
     test('non-alias merge value', () => {
       const src = '{ <<: A, B: b }'

pr.title: Include context arg in reviver calls + serialize raw JSON values
pr.body:
Adds support for the new `reviver` & `JSON.rawJSON` capabilities that were added to JS in ECMAScript 2026 by the [JSON.parse source text access](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-json-parse-with-source) proposal.

When using `parse()` or `doc.toJS()`, if a reviver is specified, it will be called with a third argument (in addition to `key` and `value`): a `context` object which contains a `source` string value for scalar values. Note that the `source` is the unescaped and unfolded string value, not the raw YAML source.

Correspondingly, during serialization, values returned by `JSON.rawJSON()` are effectively handled as strings, and so should "just work".

problem_statement:
Include context arg in reviver calls + serialize raw JSON values

Adds support for the new `reviver` & `JSON.rawJSON` capabilities that were added to JS in ECMAScript 2026 by the [JSON.parse source text access](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-json-parse-with-source) proposal.

When using `parse()` or `doc.toJS()`, if a reviver is specified, it will be called with a third argument (in addition to `key` and `value`): a `context` object which contains a `source` string value for scalar values. Note that the `source` is the unescaped and unfolded string value, not the raw YAML source.

Correspondingly, during serialization, values returned by `JSON.rawJSON()` are effectively handled as strings, and so should "just work".

diff --git a/tests/rawJSON.ts b/tests/rawJSON.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..8892995
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/rawJSON.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+import type { YAMLSeq } from 'yaml'
+import { Document, Scalar, stringify } from 'yaml'
+
+describe.runIf(JSON.rawJSON)('stringify raw JSON', () => {
+  test('quoted string', () => {
+    const raw = '"Foo\\n bar"'
+    const res = stringify(JSON.rawJSON(raw))
+    expect(res).toBe(`${raw}\n`)
+  })
+
+  test('long number in array', () => {
+    const raw = '9'.repeat(99)
+    const res = stringify([JSON.rawJSON(raw)])
+    expect(res).toBe(`- ${raw}\n`)
+  })
+})
+
+describe.runIf(JSON.rawJSON)('node creation', () => {
+  test('quoted string in constructor', () => {
+    const raw = '"Foo\\n bar"'
+    const doc = new Document<Scalar>(JSON.rawJSON(raw))
+    expect(doc.value).toBeInstanceOf(Scalar)
+    expect(JSON.isRawJSON(doc.value.value)).toBe(true)
+    expect(String(doc)).toBe(`${raw}\n`)
+  })
+
+  test('long number added to sequence', () => {
+    const raw = '9'.repeat(99)
+    const doc = new Document<YAMLSeq<any>>([])
+    doc.value.push(JSON.rawJSON(raw))
+    expect(doc.value[0]).toBeInstanceOf(Scalar)
+    expect(String(doc)).toBe(`- ${raw}\n`)
+  })
+})

pr.title: fix(parser): make reset() safe inside callbacks
pr.body: Two fixes for `reset()` being called from inside a callback: - `count chunks before invoking tokenizer callbacks`: `writeIndex` is incremented before the tokenizer runs, so a `reset()` from a callback does not leave the chunk count one behind. - `stop closing a stack reset by a callback`: the implied-close loop in `onclosetag` is bounded by the matched element's position, so a `reset()` from an `onclosetag` callback ends the loop instead of closing elements of the new document. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Fixed parser behavior when parsing is reset from a callback. Text queued after a reset is delivered in order, including when parsing pauses and resumes. Resetting during a closing-tag callback now stops additional closing-tag callbacks for the current input, preventing callbacks from continuing after parsing has been reset.

pr.title: fix(parser): recognize CDATA directly inside SVG and MathML integration points
pr.body:
Follow-up to #2458. Greptile flagged this case on that PR before it was merged ([comment](https://github.com/fb55/htmlparser2/pull/2458#discussion_r4234675969)), and it is right. That PR uses `isInForeignContext()` to decide whether `]]>` now gives a `[CDATA[x` comment followed by a live ``. Before #2458 it gave a single `[CDATA[x>]]` comment. The [markup declaration open state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#markup-declaration-open-state) switches to the CDATA section state when the adjusted current node is not an element in the HTML namespace. `foreignObject` is an SVG element, so this is a CDATA section and its content is text. whatwg/html#4016 was closed on this in July ("Gecko, WebKit, and tests match the standard"), and web-platform-tests/wpt#61253 added the tests. Chromium and parse5 still produce a comment here, so parse5 is not a usable oracle for these inputs. This adds `Parser#isCurrentNodeForeign()`, which treats an integration point as being in the namespace it was opened in, and uses it for the CDATA decision in the tokenizer and in `oncdata`. A tokenizer whose callbacks only implement `isInForeignContext` gets the same events as before, except for unclosed CDATA at the end of input (see below). The open PR #2492 adds a similar check for the element being opened, for the self-closing flag; this one is about the current node, and the two branches merge without conflicts. A second commit handles the end of input: unclosed CDATA now goes to `oncdata` when the current node is SVG or MathML, so `` | text `x>` | comment, live `` | comment, live `` | text `x>` | | `` | text `x>` | comment, live `` | comment, live `` | text `x>` | | `x><b>` | text `x>` | comment, live `` | comment, live `` | text `x>` | | `x><b>` | text `x>` | text `x>` | comment, live `` | text `x>` | | `` | comment, live `` | comment, live `` | comment, live `` | comment, live `` | The six cases from wpt#61253, run through `parseDocument` and compared with the trees in that file: master matches 3, this PR matches 6. Tests: five event tests next to the existing foreign CDATA ones. Four fail on master: `foreignObject`, `mtext` and the two unclosed-at-EOF cases. The fifth puts a `

` inside `foreignObject` and passes on both, as a check that HTML content there still gets a bogus comment. `npm run test:vi`: 205 passed, and `npm run lint` passes, after merging the current master. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Corrected CDATA handling around SVG integration points: CDATA on foreign elements is treated as text, while CDATA in their HTML content is treated as a comment. * Improved handling of CDATA within HTML paragraphs nested in SVG integration points. * Corrected handling of unclosed CDATA at the end of input in SVG content and SVG integration-point content.

pr.title: fix(parser): preserve prototype-named attributes
pr.body:
Parsing `
` emits the attribute callback but silently loses the attribute from `onopentag` and the resulting DOM. Assignment to the inherited `__proto__` setter on the attributes object does not create a string-valued own property. This also loses the attribute when the DOM is serialized. Define that attribute as an enumerable data property. Ordinary attributes keep their existing assignment path, the dictionary retains `Object.prototype`, and the first duplicate attribute still wins. Validation: three regression cases fail before the fix. `npm test` passes all 203 tests, including character-by-character HTML/XML input and DOM serialization, plus ESLint, TypeScript and Biome. `npm run build` and `git diff --check` pass. Prepared and tested with OpenAI Codex assistance. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Corrected parsing of `__proto__` attributes so they are retained as regular attributes, including when duplicate values are present. * Preserved the expected handling of `constructor` attributes and the attributes object’s standard prototype.

problem_statement:

Define that attribute as an enumerable data property. Ordinary attributes keep their existing assignment path, the dictionary retains `Object.prototype`, and the first duplicate attribute still wins. Validation: three regression cases fail before the fix. `npm test` passes all 203 tests, including character-by-character HTML/XML input and DOM serialization, plus ESLint, TypeScript and Biome. `npm run build` and `git diff --check` pass. Prepared and tested with OpenAI Codex assistance. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Corrected parsing of `__proto__` attributes so they are retained as regular attributes, including when duplicate values are present. * Preserved the expected handling of `constructor` attributes and the attributes object’s standard prototype.

pr.title: fix(stream): preserve byte order when string chunks interrupt decoding
pr.body: Both writable stream adapters accept decoded string chunks alongside binary chunks. If a UTF-8 character is incomplete when a nonempty string arrives, the decoder retains the bytes until a later binary chunk. For `[0xe2,0x82]`, `"text"`, `[0xac]`, callbacks therefore emit `text€`, moving earlier bytes after the string. Flush pending decoder bytes before nonempty string chunks in the Node and Web adapters. Empty strings retain the decoder state so they do not split a valid fragmented character. Tests pin ordering and the empty-string case for both APIs. Validation: both ordering regressions fail before the change. `npm test` passes all 204 tests plus ESLint, TypeScript and Biome; `npm run build` and `git diff --check` pass. Prepared and tested with OpenAI Codex assistance. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved UTF-8 decoding when byte and string chunks are mixed. Incomplete characters are resolved before non-empty strings, and later continuation bytes are handled correctly. Empty strings still allow buffered bytes to continue forming a character. * Corrected byte order mark handling in mixed chunks: a mark in the first byte chunk after a string chunk is preserved.

pr.title: perf(parser): answer "is this name open" with a count per name
pr.body:
#2481 made the open-element stack push/pop, which fixed deep nesting. Three lookups still read every open element, once per tag, so each one is quadratic in the nesting depth on its own: - `onclosetag` runs `this.stack.lastIndexOf(name)`. For an end tag whose name is not open, it reads the whole stack and finds nothing. - `emitOpenTag` runs `this.stack.includes("form")` on every `
`. - `readTagName` runs `this.stack.includes(adjusted)` for an SVG-cased name (`clippath`, `foreignobject`, ...) once a foreign context is open. A comment on #2481 points out the same three (https://github.com/fb55/htmlparser2/pull/2481#issuecomment-6072793486) and offers a follow-up. I haven't seen one land, so here is one. Happy to close this in favour of theirs. ## The change The parser keeps a `Map` from tag name to how many elements of that name are open. It's updated in the same three places the stack changes: push in `emitOpenTag`, pop in `popElement`, clear in `reset`. Then: - A name that is not open costs one lookup and no stack reads. - An open name is still found with `lastIndexOf` from the top. That scan only passes the elements the end tag then closes, and their open tags already paid for them. - The `` and SVG-casing checks become `openCounts.has(...)`. ## Numbers Reads of `stack`, counted with the `countArrayReads` helper the linear-work tests already use: | input | depth 500 | 1,000 | 2,000 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `
` x n, then `` x n, before | 250,499 | 1,000,999 | 4,001,999 | | after | 499 | 999 | 1,999 | | `
` x n, then `` x n, before | 250,999 | 1,001,999 | 4,003,999 | | after | 500 | 1,000 | 2,000 | | `

Parser: end tags nobody opened, repeated
and SVG-cased names still scan every open element On master (a4c60b8e0), after #2481, three lookups still read the whole open-element stack once per tag: - `onclosetag`: `this.stack.lastIndexOf(name)`, for an end tag whose name is not open. - `emitOpenTag`: `this.stack.includes("form")`, on every ``. - `readTagName`: `this.stack.includes(adjusted)`, for an SVG-cased name once a foreign context is open. Each is quadratic in the nesting depth, and a page that triggers it is small: ```js import { Parser } from "htmlparser2"; const n = 20_000; const html = "x".repeat(n) + "".repeat(n); // 156 KB const started = performance.now(); new Parser({ onclosetag() {} }).end(html); console.log(performance.now() - started); ``` Measured on a heavily loaded machine, so the ratios matter more than the absolute times: | input | n | size | master, Node 24.21 | master, Bun 1.4.2 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `x` x n, then `` x n | 10,000 | 78 KB | 6.5 s | 4.7 s | | | 20,000 | 156 KB | 23.9 s | 39.2 s | | `x` x n, then `` x n | 10,000 | 98 KB | 2.9 s | 2.8 s | | | 20,000 | 195 KB | 9.1 s | 8.5 s | | `

pr.title: fix: replace the matched placeholder, not an earlier copy inside a value
pr.body:
With the default `skipOnVariables: true`, a `{{placeholder}}` carried inside an interpolated value should stay literal. It does not when the same placeholder also appears later in the translation. `interpolate()` writes each value with `str.replace(match[0], ...)`, which replaces the first copy of the placeholder text, and by then the first copy is the one inside the earlier value:

```js
// msg: '{{name}} has {{count}} items'
i18next.t('msg', { name: '{{count}}', count: 5 });
// before: '5 has {{count}} items'
// after:  '{{count}} has 5 items'
```

This is the case reported in https://github.com/i18next/i18next/issues/1595#issuecomment-814609503.

This change slices the value in at `match.index`, the way `nest()` has done since 26.4.4. The `lastIndex` arithmetic is unchanged and now matches where the text is actually written. Slicing also keeps `$&`, `$'`, `` $` `` and `$$` literal, so `regexSafe` has no caller left and is removed. With `skipOnVariables: false` the loop restarts at 0 after every replacement, where the first copy is always the match, so those results do not change.

Two cases are added to the existing table in `test/runtime/i18next.interpolation.skipOnVariables.test.js`, one plain and one with an escaped `<...>` value. Both fail on `master` (the first returns `'value something {{b}}'`) and pass with the change.

pr.title: fix: keep placeholders inside unescaped values literal
pr.body: With the default `skipOnVariables: true`, a `{{placeholder}}` inside a value inserted with `{{- var}}` is still interpolated. `interpolate()` writes the unescaped values first, then the escape pass scans the whole string again from the start. That pass skips the values it wrote itself, but not the unescaped ones: ```js i18next.t('{{- a}}', { a: '{{b}}', b: 'c' }); // before: 'c' // after: '{{b}}' ``` This is the last case in https://github.com/i18next/i18next/issues/1595#issuecomment-814611747. It shows up when pre-built HTML that carries user text goes through `{{- html}}` next to other variables. With `emailHTML = t('{{email}}', { email })` and `t('You may contact {{name}} at {{- emailHTML}}.', { name: 'Ann', emailHTML })`, an email of `{{name}}` renders as `Ann` instead of `{{name}}`, so user text can pull another variable of the same `t()` call into the output. The unescape pass now records where it wrote each value, and the escape pass skips a match that starts inside one. Since the escape pass changes the string length to the left of its next match, it keeps that offset (`shift`) to map back to the recorded positions. With `skipOnVariables: false` nothing is recorded, so that mode and values without braces give the same output as before. I also compared the result with a single left-to-right scan over 20k random templates and values, with no differences. Three cases are added to the table in `test/runtime/i18next.interpolation.skipOnVariables.test.js`. All three fail on `master` (`'c'`, `'<b> <b>'`, `'c at c'`) and pass with the change. The third one also fails if the offset is left out. problem_statement: fix: keep placeholders inside unescaped values literal With the default `skipOnVariables: true`, a `{{placeholder}}` inside a value inserted with `{{- var}}` is still interpolated. `interpolate()` writes the unescaped values first, then the escape pass scans the whole string again from the start. That pass skips the values it wrote itself, but not the unescaped ones: ```js i18next.t('{{- a}}', { a: '{{b}}', b: 'c' }); // before: 'c' // after: '{{b}}' ``` This is the last case in https://github.com/i18next/i18next/issues/1595#issuecomment-814611747. It shows up when pre-built HTML that carries user text goes through `{{- html}}` next to other variables. With `emailHTML = t('{{email}}', { email })` and `t('You may contact {{name}} at {{- emailHTML}}.', { name: 'Ann', emailHTML })`, an email of `{{name}}` renders as `Ann` instead of `{{name}}`, so user text can pull another variable of the same `t()` call into the output. The unescape pass now records where it wrote each value, and the escape pass skips a match that starts inside one. Since the escape pass changes the string length to the left of its next match, it keeps that offset (`shift`) to map back to the recorded positions. With `skipOnVariables: false` nothing is recorded, so that mode and values without braces give the same output as before. I also compared the result with a single left-to-right scan over 20k random templates and values, with no differences. Three cases are added to the table in `test/runtime/i18next.interpolation.skipOnVariables.test.js`. All three fail on `master` (`'c'`, `'<b> <b>'`, `'c at c'`) and pass with the change. The third one also fails if the offset is left out. pr.title: fix: copy nested resources when cloning with forkResourceStore
pr.body:
`cloneInstance({ forkResourceStore: true })` copies the store data only down to the namespace objects, so everything below that is still shared with the original instance. `addResource()` on a nested key and a deep `addResourceBundle()` write into those shared objects in place, so a change made on the fork also shows up in the original instance and in every other fork:

```js
const parent = i18next.createInstance();
await parent.init({ lng: 'en', resources: { en: { translation: { greeting: { hello: 'Hello' } } } } });

const fork = parent.cloneInstance({ forkResourceStore: true });
fork.addResource('en', 'translation', 'greeting.hello', 'Hi');
parent.t('greeting.hello'); // before: 'Hi', after: 'Hello'

const fork2 = parent.cloneInstance({ forkResourceStore: true });
fork2.addResourceBundle('en', 'translation', { greeting: { bye: 'Bye' } }, true, true);
parent.t('greeting.bye'); // before: 'Bye', after: 'greeting.bye'
```

Apps hit this when they fork to hold per-instance overrides with nested keys. [frak-id/wallet](https://github.com/frak-id/wallet/blob/a3592a06a05230af157ff0c9fda078a10e5ab4e0/apps/wallet/app/module/sharing/component/SharingView.tsx) keeps its per-merchant overrides out of i18next for this reason: its comment notes that a deep `addResourceBundle` on the fork writes through to the shared instance. Flat keys were already isolated, which is the case the existing test covers.

The fork now copies every object and array level of the store data. Arrays are copied too, because `deepExtend` merges them index by index. Strings are still shared. It stays faster than the JSON round trip in the comment: with 15k keys in 1,500 nested groups, one fork takes about 1.0 ms instead of 0.3 ms, against 3.2 ms for `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify())`.

The new test in `test/runtime/i18next.test.js` makes a nested `addResource` and a deep `addResourceBundle` on a fork and checks that the original keeps its values, including an array. It fails on `master` (`expected 'value here cloned' to equal 'value here'`), passes with the change, and also fails if arrays are not copied.

Ran: `npm test` (52 files, 1012 passed, 9 skipped), `npm run test:typescript`, `npm run test:coverage` on Node 24
Checked: `npm run format`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`

pr.title: fix: format values when cached formatter options are not serializable
pr.body:
With the default `cacheInBuiltFormats: true`, a BigInt value is printed unformatted, while the same call with `cacheInBuiltFormats: false` formats it (`Intl.NumberFormat` supports BigInt):

```js
await i18next.init({ lng: 'en', resources: { en: { translation: { num: 'Total: {{val, number}}' } } } });

i18next.t('num', { val: 12345678901234567890n });
// before: 'Total: 12345678901234567890'
// after:  'Total: 12,345,678,901,234,567,890' (same as with cacheInBuiltFormats: false)
```

The cached formatter builds its cache key with `JSON.stringify` over all t() options, and the interpolation values are part of them. `JSON.stringify` throws on a BigInt or on a circular object, `Formatter.format` catches the error and only logs it as a warning, so every built-in format in that call (number, currency, datetime, relativetime, list and `addCached` formatters) returns the raw value. This is easy to hit with BigInt ids, balances or block numbers (Prisma `BigInt` columns, viem/ethers), or when an object with a back-reference, such as an ORM entity, is passed as interpolation data: `t('greet', { user, val: 1234.5 })` with `'Hi {{user.name}}, total {{val, number}}'` gives `total 1234.5` when `user.self = user`. Circular objects in t() options are otherwise supported: #875 removed the same kind of `JSON.stringify` call from nesting for this reason.

When the key cannot be built, the formatter now formats without the cache, the same way `cacheInBuiltFormats: false` does. Options that serialize take the same cached path as before, and errors thrown by the format function itself are still caught and logged by `Formatter.format`. The cache key still includes the value, so the memory behaviour discussed in #2227 is unchanged.

The new test in `test/runtime/i18next.translation.formatting.test.js` formats a BigInt and a value next to a circular object. It fails on `master` (`expected 'Some 12345678901234567890' to deeply equal 'Some 12,345,678,901,234,567,890'`) and passes with the change.

Ran: `npm test` (52 files, 1013 passed, 9 skipped), `npm run test:typescript`, `npm run test:coverage` on Node 24
Checked: `npm run format`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`

pr.title: fix: don't interpolate inherited methods like constructor from nested values
pr.body:
Nested interpolation values resolve to inherited methods:

```js
i18next.t('greeting', { user: { name: 'Bob' } }) // greeting: "Hi {{user.constructor}}!"
// "Hi function Object() { [native code] }!"
// "{{user.toString}}" -> "function toString() { [native code] }", "{{items.map}}" -> the Array method
```

At the top level the same key is treated as missing (`{{constructor}}` -> missing value), because `deepFind` checks `hasOwnProperty` on its first `obj[path]` lookup, and `getPath` does too. The nested loop just read `current[nextPath]`.

The nested loop now treats an inherited function as missing. I didn't add a plain `hasOwnProperty` check, because getters on class instances (`{{user.fullName}}` with `get fullName()` on the prototype) are inherited too and should keep working. A test covers that.

Tests: `#deepFind` cases in `test/runtime/utils.test.js` and two interpolation cases in `test/runtime/interpolation.test.js`. They fail on master, and the full runtime suite passes (717 tests).

pr.title: fix: don't match a supported language that only starts with the same letters
pr.body:
When none of the detected codes is in `supportedLngs`, `getBestMatchFromCodes` ends with a fuzzy lookup over `supportedLngs`, and its last check was `supportedLng.startsWith(lngOnly)` with no boundary. A different language whose code merely starts with the same letters gets picked:

```js
i18next.init({ supportedLngs: ['en', 'fil-PH'], fallbackLng: 'en', lng: 'fi-FI' })
i18next.language // 'fil-PH': a Finnish user gets Filipino instead of the fallback

// ha (Hausa) -> haw-US (Hawaiian), same thing
```

`lngOnly` comes from `getLanguagePartFromCode` and never contains a `-`. So the check just above (`supportedLng.slice(0, supportedLng.indexOf('-')) === lngOnly`) already covers "same language, other region" (`de-CH` -> `de-DE`, `fil` -> `fil-PH`). The `startsWith` line could only add matches that cross a language boundary, so I removed it.

Added a `getBestMatchFromCodes()` suite to `test/runtime/languageUtils.test.js`: `fi-FI` / `ha` fall back to `en`, while `fil` -> `fil-PH` and `pt-PT` -> `pt-BR` still match. The first two fail on master, and the full runtime suite passes (721 tests).

pr.title: fix: preserve falsy nested resource values
pr.body:
## Problem

When a nested resource value is `false`, `0`, or `''` and a flat key with the same dotted name also exists, `getResource('en', 'translation', 'a.b')` returns the flat value. These are present values, not missing keys; for example, `Translator.isValidLookup` accepts `false` and `0`.

## Fix

Only fall back to flat-key lookup when the nested result is `undefined`. Apply the same presence check to the dotted lookup form. A parameterized regression test covers both access forms and all three falsy values.

## Tests

- `npm run test:runtime -- --run test/runtime/resourceStore.fallback.test.js` — 4 passed; 3 new cases failed before the fix for the expected reason.
- `npm test` — 1029 passed, 9 skipped.
- `npm run test:typescript` — 534 passed, no type errors.
- `npm run lint` — passed.
- `npm run format` — passed.
- `npm run build` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

## Compatibility

Flat-key fallback when a nested path is absent remains unchanged. The behavior changes only for colliding keys whose nested value exists but is falsy.

## Related issue

No linked issue; reproduced on current `master` and checked against open PRs before submission.

pr.title: fix: preserve caller options when forking instances
pr.body:
Reusing `{ forkResourceStore: true }` with `cloneInstance()` silently stops forking after the first call because the method deletes the flag from the caller's object. A second clone then shares the parent store, so changing its translation also changes the parent. Passing frozen fork options throws instead.

I copy the options inside the existing fork branch before removing its private flag. Tests cover two clones made with the same options, frozen options, and the existing false/undefined shared-store behavior.

Validation on Node 24.19.0/macOS arm64: 1,035 runtime/compatibility tests passed, nine skipped; 534 type tests passed; lint, configured formatting and build passed. Coverage recorded 95.23% lines. Full suites use process-scoped `TZ=UTC`; the same three pre-existing local date-format failures occur on the original and changed code under the host Toronto timezone. Both packed CJS/ESM exports reproduce the corrected behavior outside the checkout.

#### Checklist

- [x] only relevant code is changed (diff reviewed before submission)
- [x] run tests `npm run test` (process-scoped `TZ=UTC`, as described above)
- [x] tests are included
- [x] commit message and code follows the [Developer's Certification of Origin](https://github.com/i18next/.github/blob/98c457fcbcd1bac8a151ec51e905d7d1dba735b3/CONTRIBUTING.md)

pr.title: fix: keep nested 0, false and '' interpolation values with a custom keySeparator
pr.body:
With `keySeparator: false` (or a custom separator such as `'::'` or `'/'`), a nested interpolation value that is `0`, `false` or `''` is not inserted. Truthy values and the default `'.'` separator work:

```js
await i18next.init({
  lng: 'en',
  keySeparator: false,
  resources: { en: { translation: { unread: 'You have {{stats.unread}} unread messages' } } },
});

i18next.t('unread', { stats: { unread: 0 } });
// before: 'You have {{stats.unread}} unread messages'
// after:  'You have 0 unread messages'
```

Apps hit this when they use flat or natural-language keys and pass an object as interpolation data: an unread count of 0, a `false` flag, an empty `{{user.middle}}`. Formatted values go through the same lookup, so `'Total: {{order.total, currency(USD)}}'` with a total of 0 also keeps the placeholder, and so do nested `defaultVariables`. With `skipOnVariables: false` the value becomes `''` with a "missed to pass in variable" warning.

`deepFindWithDefaults` finds the value with `getPathWithDefaults`, which splits on `.`, but the `!path` check treats any falsy result as missing and looks again with `deepFind(data, key, keySeparator)`. With `'.'` that finds the same value; with `false` or `'::'` it does not split `stats.unread` and returns `undefined`. The fallback now only runs when nothing was found, like the check #2461 changed in `ResourceStore.getResource`. `null` stays a found value, as it already is with `'.'` (`{ test: null }` renders `''` and overrides `defaultVariables`). Flat dotted data keys (`{ 'a.b': 0 }`) still resolve through `deepFind`; only when the same name exists both nested and flat does the nested falsy value now win, as a truthy one already does.

The new test in `test/runtime/interpolation.test.js` runs with `false` and `'::'`. It fails on `master` (received `'{{stats.unread}}|{{stats.muted}}|{{stats.label}}|3|flat'`, expected `'0|false||3|flat'`) and passes with the change.

Ran: `npm test` (52 files, 1037 passed, 9 skipped), `npm run test:typescript`, `npm run test:coverage` on Node 24
Checked: `npm run format`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`

pr.title: fix: keep at most 1000 formatters in each cached format
pr.body:
With the default `cacheInBuiltFormats: true`, every new value that goes through a format keeps a formatter for good:

```js
const i18n = i18next.createInstance();
i18n.init({ lng: 'en', initAsync: false, resources: { en: { translation: { price: 'Price {{amount, currency(USD)}}' } } } });
for (let i = 0; i < 100000; i++) i18n.t('price', { amount: i });
// heap after gc: +49.8 MB on 27.0.0 (and on 26.5.3), +0.8 MB with this change
```

The cache key of `createCachedFormatter` is the language plus `JSON.stringify` of all t() options, and the options hold the interpolated values. So each new amount, date or name adds an entry, and nothing is ever removed. This applies to all built-in formats (number, currency, datetime, relativetime, list) and to `addCached`. In a browser tab this rarely matters, but a server that renders pages for days with ever new prices, dates or user names grows without end. The change in #2227 drops the value from the key only when `formatParams` names it, which most calls do not.

Each cached format now keeps at most 1000 formatters in a `Map` and drops the oldest one when it is full. A dropped formatter is made again from the same language and options, so the output is the same. Keys that repeat stay cached as before.

The new test in `test/runtime/formatter.cache.test.js` formats 5000 values through an `addCached` format, counts how often the factory runs, and checks that a recent value is still cached while the first one is made again. It fails on `master` (the first value is never made again) and passes with the change.

Ran the `test` (54 files, 1101 passed, 9 skipped), `test:typescript`, `lint` and `build` scripts, and prettier on the changed files, on Node 24.

#### Checklist

- [x] only relevant code is changed (make a diff before you submit the PR)
- [x] run tests `npm run test`
- [x] tests are included
- [ ] documentation is changed or added
